passageTitle: 'Cambridge IELTS 19 – Academic Reading Full Test', passageText: `PASSAGE 1: DIRECT AIR CAPTURE & THE RACE FOR NET-ZERO Direct Air Capture (DAC) refers to chemical technologies designed to extract carbon dioxide molecules directly from ambient atmospheric air, distinct from point-source capture at industrial smokestacks. Because atmospheric CO₂ concentration is exceedingly diffuse — approximately 420 parts per million (0.04%) — capturing a single metric ton requires processing over two million cubic meters of ambient air through specialised sorbent materials. Proponents emphasise that DAC provides an indispensable mechanism to neutralise emissions from hard-to-abate sectors such as commercial aviation, long-haul maritime shipping, and heavy metallurgy. Unlike renewable energy or fuel switching, DAC directly addresses the stock of atmospheric CO₂ that has already accumulated over more than a century of industrial activity. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) considers carbon dioxide removal — of which DAC is the most scalable technological form — a necessary component of limiting global warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels. However, prominent environmental economists express scepticism regarding energy parasitic loads. Operating DAC facilities at gigaton scale would demand substantial quantities of dedicated renewable electricity — some estimates suggest 100–300 kWh per metric ton — potentially diverting clean power away from immediate grid decarbonisation efforts. Swiss company Climeworks and Canadian firm Carbon Engineering have demonstrated commercial-scale pilots, but current costs range from $400–$1,000 per tonne. Analysts forecast that levelised costs must decline from current levels to under $100 per tonne before voluntary carbon offset markets can sustain autonomous industrial deployment without substantial government subsidies. Technological breakthroughs in solid sorbent materials and modular electrochemical cell design are expected to drive this cost reduction. PASSAGE 2: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN DIAGNOSTIC RADIOLOGY The integration of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) into diagnostic radiology has achieved diagnostic accuracy rates rivalling, and in specific pathology subsets exceeding, senior medical specialists. Algorithms trained on millions of annotated radiographic images demonstrate exceptional fidelity in detecting early malignant neoplasms, pulmonary nodules, and subtle trabecular micro-fractures. The technology's trajectory has been steep. In 2012, AlexNet demonstrated that deep learning could classify images with unprecedented accuracy. By 2017, Stanford University's CheXNet surpassed radiologist performance in detecting pneumonia from chest X-rays. By 2020, multiple peer-reviewed studies confirmed CNN performance at or above human expert level in screening for diabetic retinopathy, colorectal cancer polyps, and dermatological malignancies. Despite algorithmic triumphs, biomedical ethicists point to the intractable "black box" problem. Deep neural architectures process millions of weighted parameters across hidden layers, rendering it virtually impossible to reconstruct the exact causal reasoning underpinning a specific clinical determination. When an AI generates a false-positive diagnosis that initiates invasive biopsy procedures, legal attribution of liability remains fiercely contested between software manufacturers, medical institutions, and attending physicians. Furthermore, dataset bias represents a chronic vulnerability. When predictive models are trained predominantly on demographic cohorts from high-income urban medical centres, their predictive validity deteriorates sharply when evaluating pathologies among historically underrepresented rural populations. A 2022 systematic review in The Lancet Digital Health found that AI diagnostic tools performed, on average, 14% less accurately for patients from low-income countries compared to their training cohort benchmarks. PASSAGE 3: THE EVOLUTIONARY ORIGINS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE The capacity for human language represents one of the most debated questions in evolutionary biology and cognitive science. Unlike anatomical traits preserved in the fossil record, language leaves no direct physical evidence, compelling researchers to rely on indirect proxies: the morphology of vocal tract bones, the archaeological record of symbolic behaviour, and comparative studies of primate communication. Fossil evidence suggests that the hyoid bone — a U-shaped bone in the throat essential for complex vocalisation — reached its modern human configuration approximately 300,000 years ago in Homo heidelbergensis. However, possession of an anatomically modern vocal apparatus does not automatically confer linguistic capacity; the neural machinery for syntax, recursion, and semantic displacement appears to have developed later. The archaeological record provides additional clues. Ochre processing, shell bead jewellery, and engraved geometric patterns appear in the archaeological record as far back as 100,000 years ago in South Africa, suggesting the emergence of symbolic thinking — widely regarded as a prerequisite for fully compositional language. The 'cultural explosion' evident in European sites approximately 40,000 years ago — with its sudden proliferation of cave art, flutes crafted from bird bone, and figurative statuettes — may represent the crystallisation of modern linguistic cognition. Noam Chomsky's influential theory of Universal Grammar posits that humans possess an innate neurological endowment — a 'language acquisition device' — that predisposes children to identify grammatical rules across all natural human languages regardless of cultural context. Critics, notably Daniel Everett, challenge this nativist paradigm by arguing that Amazonian languages such as Pirahã demonstrate neither recursion nor embedded clauses, suggesting that grammatical complexity is culturally transmitted rather than biologically innate.`, questions: [ // PASSAGE 1 (Q1–7) { text: 'What percentage of atmospheric concentration represents current CO₂ levels?', translated: 'Nồng độ CO₂ trong khí quyển hiện tại chiếm bao nhiêu phần trăm?', choices: ['0.02%', '0.04%', '0.40%', '4.00%'], answer: 1, ai_explain: '"atmospheric CO₂ concentration is exceedingly diffuse — approximately 420 parts per million (0.04%)".' }, { text: 'According to the IPCC, what role does carbon dioxide removal play in limiting global warming?', translated: 'Theo IPCC, việc loại bỏ CO₂ đóng vai trò gì trong việc hạn chế biến đổi khí hậu?', choices: ['It is optional if renewable energy is scaled sufficiently', 'It is a necessary component to limit warming to 1.5°C', 'It should replace all fossil fuel combustion immediately', 'It is irrelevant to current emissions targets'], answer: 1, ai_explain: '"The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) considers carbon dioxide removal — a necessary component of limiting global warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels."' }, { text: 'The current cost of Direct Air Capture technology ranges from $400 to $1,000 per tonne.', translated: 'Chi phí hiện tại của DAC dao động từ $400 đến $1,000 mỗi tấn.', choices: ['TRUE', 'FALSE', 'NOT GIVEN'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'TRUE. "current costs range from $400–$1,000 per tonne" — được ghi nhận rõ ràng.' }, { text: 'DAC technology is most effective when deployed specifically at coal power plant exhaust systems.', translated: 'Công nghệ DAC hiệu quả nhất khi triển khai tại hệ thống xả thải của các nhà máy điện than.', choices: ['TRUE', 'FALSE', 'NOT GIVEN'], answer: 1, ai_explain: 'FALSE. Task 1 + Task 2 (Bài mẫu Band 8.5)': { type: 'writing', questions: [ { text: 'IELTS Academic Writing Task 1 (20 phút – ≥150 từ): The bar chart below shows the proportion of electricity generated from renewable sources across five European countries (Germany, France, Denmark, Spain, and Norway) in 2015 and 2023. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.', translated: 'Biểu đồ cột mô tả tỷ lệ điện năng sản xuất từ nguồn tái tạo tại 5 quốc gia châu Âu giai đoạn 2015–2023. Tóm tắt các đặc điểm chính có so sánh.', choices: [ '📋 DÀN Ý CHUẨN BAND 8.0: (1) Overview: overall, all five nations recorded growth with Norway and Denmark leading; (2) Body 1: Germany rose from 28% to 51%; France from 15% to 26%; (3) Body 2: Denmark achieved the highest increase (38%→79%), Norway already high (61%→74%), Spain showed moderate growth (18%→44%); (4) Kết luận: renewables expansion driven by wind/solar policy.', '✍️ BÀI MẪU BAND 8.5 THAM KHẢO: "The bar chart delineates the trajectory of electricity generation from renewable sources across five European nations in 2015 and 2023. Overall, it is immediately apparent that all five countries recorded upward trajectories, with Denmark and Norway consistently representing the highest proportions throughout the illustrated period, while France lagged notably behind its counterparts. In 2015, Norway already derived the majority of its electricity from renewables at 61%, followed by Denmark at 38% and Germany at 28%. By contrast, France and Spain contributed comparatively modest shares of 15% and 18% respectively. Over the subsequent eight years, the most dramatic transformation occurred in Denmark, whose renewable proportion surged by 41 percentage points to reach 79% in 2023 — the highest among all nations. Germany recorded a substantial increase to 51%, reflecting its ambitious Energiewende energy transition policy. Spain more than doubled its share from 18% to 44%, driven principally by solar photovoltaic expansion. Norway, already a hydropower-dominant economy, recorded a comparatively restrained rise to 74%. France, by contrast, achieved the smallest absolute growth, advancing marginally from 15% to 26%. In summary, while all five nations expanded their renewable electricity generation capacity, Denmark and Norway emerged as continental leaders, whereas France demonstrated the least progress over the period." [ĐẠT: Band 8.5 – Lexical Resource C1, Coherence & Cohesion, Grammar Accuracy]', '🎯 TIÊU CHÍ CHẤM BAND 8.5: Task Achievement (đủ thông tin + overview rõ) + Coherence & Cohesion (liên từ chuyên nghiệp) + Lexical Resource (delineates, trajectory, marginally, Energiewende) + Grammatical Range & Accuracy (passive voice, relative clauses, comparison structures)' ], answer: 1, ai_explain: 'Task 1 Band 8.5 cần: Overview 2 xu hướng chính, phân nhóm các nước theo mức độ tăng, dùng từ ngữ so sánh chính xác và không có lỗi ngữ pháp.' }, { text: 'IELTS Academic Writing Task 2 (40 phút – ≥250 từ): Some people believe that the increasing use of technology and social media is weakening human relationships and communication skills. Others argue that technology enables people to build stronger and more diverse connections than ever before. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.', translated: 'Task 2: Một số người cho rằng việc sử dụng công nghệ và mạng xã hội ngày càng nhiều đang làm suy yếu các mối quan hệ và kỹ năng giao tiếp của con người. Người khác lập luận rằng công nghệ cho phép xây dựng các kết nối đa dạng và bền chặt hơn. Thảo luận cả hai quan điểm và nêu ý kiến của bạn.', choices: [ '📋 DÀN Ý 4 ĐOẠN BAND 8.0: Introduction: Paraphrase + thesis (although concerns are valid, technology ultimately strengthens human connection when used mindfully). Body 1: Concerns about tech (phubbing, social comparison anxiety, reduced empathy in text-based communication). Body 2: Benefits (diaspora families maintaining bonds, professional networking, access to global support communities, e.g., mental health forums). Conclusion: Balanced + restated opinion.', '✍️ BÀI MẪU BAND 8.5 THAM KHẢO: "In an era defined by relentless digital innovation, a contentious pedagogical and sociological debate has emerged concerning technology\'s net impact on human interpersonal dynamics. While a faction of social commentators decry the corrosive effects of screen-mediated communication on authentic human connection, I fundamentally contend that technology, when wielded with intentionality, enhances rather than diminishes our capacity for meaningful relationship formation. Proponents of the restrictive view marshal compelling evidence. Neuropsychological research published in the Journal of Social and Personal Relationships indicates that individuals who habitually check their smartphones during face-to-face conversations — a phenomenon colloquially termed \'phubbing\' — engender significant feelings of ostracism and relational dissatisfaction in their conversational partners. Furthermore, the algorithmically curated nature of social media platforms amplifies social comparison, a documented antecedent of anxiety and depression, potentially inhibiting vulnerability — the bedrock of genuine intimacy. Conversely, to characterise technology as axiomatically antithetical to human connection is to ignore compelling counterevidence. Platforms such as Zoom and WhatsApp have proven indispensable for geographically dispersed families who would otherwise be consigned to quarterly correspondence. Online communities coalesced around shared chronic illnesses, minority identities, and professional interests provide participants with targeted social support inaccessible within their immediate geographical context. Moreover, multilingual translation capabilities now enable cross-cultural friendships that previous generations could simply not have sustained. In summation, I maintain that the technology-connection dichotomy is fundamentally false. The determinative variable is not technological adoption per se, but rather the quality of intentionality and digital literacy that individuals bring to their interactions. Societies that invest in digital wellbeing education will harvest technology\'s connective dividends while mitigating its documented interpersonal costs." (328 từ — Band 8.5)', '🎯 PHÂN TÍCH TIÊU CHÍ BAND 8.5: ✅ Task Response: Thảo luận cả 2 quan điểm + nêu rõ lập trường ✅ Coherence: 4 đoạn rõ ràng, liên từ học thuật (Conversely, Furthermore, In summation) ✅ Lexical Resource: pedagogical, corrosive, ostracism, antithetical, coalesced, consigned ✅ Grammar: Complex sentences, subjunctive, passive, relative clauses' ], answer: 1, ai_explain: 'Task 2 Band 8.5 yêu cầu lập luận học thuật sâu, từ vựng C1, cấu trúc câu đa dạng phức tạp và thể hiện rõ ràng quan điểm cá nhân.' }, { text: 'BAND SCORING BREAKDOWN – SELF ASSESSMENT: Sau khi hoàn thành cả Task 1 và Task 2, hãy đánh giá bài viết của bạn theo 4 tiêu chí chấm điểm IELTS Writing chính thức.', translated: 'Tự đánh giá bài viết theo 4 tiêu chí IELTS Writing.', choices: [ '📊 TIÊU CHÍ 1 – TASK ACHIEVEMENT (TA): Band 9: Đề bài được giải quyết hoàn toàn, Overview rõ ràng và chính xác, tất cả thông tin quan trọng được nêu; Band 7: Đề bài được đề cập đầy đủ, tuy nhiên một số thông tin có thể thiếu hoặc không đủ rõ ràng.', '📊 TIÊU CHÍ 2 – COHERENCE & COHESION (CC): Band 9: Sắp xếp thông tin logic, sử dụng liên từ nhuần nhuyễn, không có lỗi; Band 7: Bố cục nhìn chung rõ ràng, đôi khi sử dụng liên từ chưa thật tự nhiên.', '📊 TIÊU CHÍ 3 & 4 – LEXICAL RESOURCE & GRAMMAR: Band 9: Từ vựng phong phú đa dạng, kiểm soát ngữ pháp hoàn toàn; Band 7: Từ vựng đủ rộng, ngữ pháp nhìn chung chính xác với một vài lỗi không ảnh hưởng đến thông điệp.' ], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Thang điểm IELTS Writing Band 6.0→9.0 dựa trên 4 tiêu chí với tỷ lệ đều nhau 25% mỗi tiêu chí: TA + CC + LR + GRA.' } ] }, // =========================================================== // CAMBRIDGE IELTS 19 – FULL SPEAKING (PART 1 + 2 + 3, 11 CÂU) // =========================================================== 'Cambridge IELTS 19 · Full Speaking Test (Part 1 + Part 2 + Part 3)': { type: 'speaking', questions: [ // PART 1 – Introduction & Interview (5 câu) { text: 'Part 1, Question 1: Do you currently study or work? Tell me about what you do.', translated: 'Part 1: Bạn đang học hay đi làm? Hãy kể về công việc/học tập của bạn.', choices: ['💡 Gợi ý 3-4 câu: State what you do → specific detail → what you enjoy → future goal. E.g., "I\'m currently in my third year studying Environmental Engineering at... What I find particularly rewarding is the laboratory component, where we design water filtration systems. Looking forward, I hope to work in sustainable urban infrastructure."', '🎯 Từ vựng band cao: pursuing a degree in, specialising in, particularly rewarding, collaborative, hands-on experience, aspire to'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Part 1 cần trả lời 2-3 câu tự nhiên, lưu loát. Tránh trả lời Yes/No đơn độc.' }, { text: 'Part 1, Question 2: Do you enjoy reading books? What kind of books do you like most?', translated: 'Part 1: Bạn có thích đọc sách không? Bạn thích thể loại sách nào nhất?', choices: ['💡 Cấu trúc lý tưởng: Direct answer (Frankly, I\'m an avid reader) → Genre preference + reason (historical non-fiction because it contextualises current events) → Recent book (Just finished "Sapiens" by Yuval Noah Harari) → Link to habit (I try to read before bed for 30 minutes as a mindfulness practice).', '🎯 Từ vựng: avid reader, voracious appetite for, captivating narrative, broaden my perspective, immerse myself in'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Liên kết câu trả lời với trải nghiệm cá nhân giúp bài nói tự nhiên và thuyết phục hơn.' }, { text: 'Part 1, Question 3: How important are friendships to you, and how do you maintain close friendships?', translated: 'Part 1: Tình bạn quan trọng như thế nào với bạn và bạn duy trì tình bạn thân thiết như thế nào?', choices: ['💡 Expand with: personal value (friendships are the cornerstone of my psychological wellbeing) → practical maintenance strategies (weekly video calls, annual trips, shared hobby groups) → specific example (my university flatmates – despite living in different cities, we have a standing Sunday call).', '🎯 Từ vựng: cornerstone of, nurture relationships, reciprocal, emotionally invested, standing commitment, geographically dispersed'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Part 1 câu về quan hệ xã hội: nêu giá trị cá nhân + chiến lược cụ thể + ví dụ thực tế.' }, { text: 'Part 1, Question 4: Do you prefer spending time indoors or outdoors? Why?', translated: 'Part 1: Bạn thích ở trong nhà hay ngoài trời? Tại sao?', choices: ['💡 Structure: State preference → 2 reasons → contrast (although I appreciate... I tend to lean toward...) → seasonal variation (In summer, I gravitate toward outdoor activities; during winter months, I retreat to indoor creative pursuits like cooking or painting).', '🎯 Từ vựng: gravitate toward, predominantly, therapeutic, restorative, seasonal variation, invigorating'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Câu hỏi sở thích không cần câu trả lời đúng/sai — quan trọng là lập luận rõ ràng và từ vựng đa dạng.' }, { text: 'Part 1, Question 5: How has your hometown changed since you were a child?', translated: 'Part 1: Quê hương của bạn đã thay đổi như thế nào kể từ khi bạn còn nhỏ?', choices: ['💡 Template: When I was growing up → specific changes (urbanisation, new infrastructure, demographic shifts) → personal feeling (bittersweet – progress brings modernisation but erases familiar cultural landmarks) → example (the traditional market replaced by a shopping complex).', '🎯 Từ vựng: bittersweet, rapid urbanisation, modernisation, demographic shifts, cultural landmarks, nostalgic'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Câu hỏi về nơi sinh – dùng thì quá khứ để so sánh và kết hợp cảm xúc cá nhân để bài nói sinh động.' }, // PART 2 – Cue Card (1 câu, 2 phút) { text: 'Part 2 – Cue Card (1 phút chuẩn bị, 2 phút nói): Describe a person who has inspired you in your life. You should say: • Who this person is / was; • How you know or knew this person; • What qualities make them inspiring; and explain • Why this person has had such a significant impact on your life.', translated: 'Part 2 Cue Card: Miêu tả một người đã truyền cảm hứng cho bạn trong cuộc sống. Nêu: người đó là ai, bạn quen họ như thế nào, những phẩm chất truyền cảm hứng, và tại sao họ có ảnh hưởng lớn với bạn.', choices: ['✍️ BÀI MẪU BAND 8.0 (2 PHÚT): "The person who has most profoundly influenced my personal trajectory is my secondary school science teacher, Mr. Nguyen Van Minh. I was fortunate to have him as my chemistry and biology teacher during my formative teenage years, a period when I was struggling to identify a sense of academic direction. What distinguished Mr. Minh from other educators was his extraordinary capacity to contextualise abstract scientific concepts within the lens of real-world environmental challenges. Rather than presenting chemistry as a series of equations to be memorised, he framed every experiment as a small piece of a larger puzzle about sustainability and human survival. I distinctly recall a pivotal class in Year 10 where he set up a water purification demonstration using locally sourced materials — it transformed my perception of science from an academic exercise into a vehicle for genuine social impact. Beyond his pedagogical brilliance, what I find most inspiring about him is his authentic intellectual humility. Despite his considerable expertise, he consistently encouraged us to challenge prevailing theories and to treat uncertainty as an invitation for further inquiry rather than as intellectual failure. His mentorship instilled in me not merely scientific knowledge, but a lifelong epistemological disposition — a genuine enthusiasm for asking questions that others might dismiss as too fundamental. I attribute my decision to study Environmental Engineering, and my aspiration to contribute to clean water access in rural communities, directly to the intellectual seeds he planted during those formative classroom hours." (243 từ — Band 8.0+)', '🎯 PHÂN TÍCH CUE CARD BAND 8.0: ✅ Fluency: Nói liên tục 2 phút không ngập ngừng dài ✅ All 4 bullet points covered ✅ Specific anecdote (water purification class) ✅ Vocabulary: profound, trajectory, formative, pedagogical, epistemological, instilled ✅ Grammar: past perfect, relative clauses, passive voice'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Cue Card Part 2: Viết ra 5-7 từ khóa trong 1 phút chuẩn bị. Mở đầu bằng "The person who..." và kết thúc bằng lý do tác động lâu dài.' }, // PART 3 – Two-way Discussion (5 câu) { text: 'Part 3, Question 1: In your opinion, do educational systems today adequately nurture and celebrate exceptional talent, or do they tend to produce conformity?', translated: 'Part 3: Theo bạn, hệ thống giáo dục hiện nay có nuôi dưỡng và tôn vinh tài năng xuất sắc đúng mức không, hay có xu hướng tạo ra sự đồng nhất?', choices: ['💡 Structure lập luận Band 8.0: Acknowledge both sides → state position → evidence 1 (standardised testing disadvantages creative divergent thinkers — Howard Gardner\'s Multiple Intelligences theory) → evidence 2 (exceptional outliers like Gates, Zuckerberg dropped out, suggesting institutional misalignment) → nuanced conclusion (systems that integrate project-based learning and individual mentorship show more promise).', '🎯 Từ vựng học thuật: standardised assessment, divergent thinking, conformity, nurture exceptionalism, pedagogical flexibility, Multiple Intelligences, institutional alignment'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Part 3 đánh giá khả năng phân tích trừu tượng, lập luận đa chiều. Không trả lời một chiều hoàn toàn.' }, { text: 'Part 3, Question 2: How do you think the relationship between teachers and students has changed over the past few decades?', translated: 'Part 3: Mối quan hệ giữa giáo viên và học sinh đã thay đổi như thế nào trong vài thập kỷ qua?', choices: ['💡 Lập luận đa chiều: Traditional model (hierarchical authority, teacher as sole knowledge custodian) → Contemporary shift (collaborative, student-centred, flipped classroom) → Role of internet (students can access expert knowledge independently, challenging teacher authority) → Risk (students may lack guidance in information literacy) → Ideal balance (teacher as facilitator and critical thinking coach).', '🎯 Từ vựng: hierarchical, facilitator, student-centred, flipped classroom, information literacy, collaborative, critical thinking coach'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'So sánh theo trục thời gian quá khứ-hiện tại là cách tiếp cận chuẩn cho các câu Part 3 về thay đổi xã hội.' }, { text: 'Part 3, Question 3: To what extent do you think success in life is determined by formal education, as opposed to natural talent or personal drive?', translated: 'Part 3: Theo bạn, thành công trong cuộc sống được quyết định ở mức độ nào bởi giáo dục chính quy, so với tài năng thiên bẩm hay động lực cá nhân?', choices: ['💡 Approach: Reject false trichotomy → argue for interaction model → Evidence: Formal education provides social networks and credentialing (Signalling Theory of Education) → Natural talent without cultivation rarely flourishes (deliberate practice research by K.A. Ericsson) → Personal drive is the binding catalyst → "grit" research by Angela Duckworth → Conclusion: Formal education is a facilitator, not a determinant.', '🎯 Từ vựng: determinant, trichotomy, credentialing, Signalling Theory, deliberate practice, grit, catalyst, facilitator'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Câu hỏi to what extent cần định lượng tương đối các yếu tố và cung cấp bằng chứng/ví dụ học thuật.' }, { text: 'Part 3, Question 4: Do you believe it is the responsibility of schools or parents to teach children values and moral behaviour?', translated: 'Part 3: Bạn có tin rằng trách nhiệm dạy giá trị và đạo đức cho trẻ em thuộc về nhà trường hay cha mẹ?', choices: ['💡 Lập luận: Both have complementary roles (false dichotomy critique) → Home is the primary moral formation environment (attachment theory, early childhood) → Schools reinforce and systematise values across diverse social contexts → Risk when values diverge between home and school → Positive case: Schools that incorporate social-emotional learning (SEL) curricula show measurable improvements in prosocial behaviour.', '🎯 Từ vựng: moral formation, complementary, prosocial, social-emotional learning (SEL), attachment theory, systematise, diverge'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Câu hỏi về trách nhiệm (responsibility): luôn thể hiện quan điểm "cả hai cùng có vai trò bổ sung cho nhau" để đạt điểm cao về reasoning.' }, { text: 'Part 3, Question 5: In your view, should governments prioritise funding for arts education or STEM subjects in schools? Justify your position.', translated: 'Part 3: Theo bạn, chính phủ nên ưu tiên tài trợ cho giáo dục nghệ thuật hay các môn STEM trong trường học? Hãy biện hộ cho lập trường của bạn.', choices: ['💡 STEM argument: Economic productivity, technological innovation, global competitiveness, employment pipeline; Arts argument: Critical thinking, cultural cohesion, mental health, creativity that drives innovation even in STEM fields → Integration argument: Countries like Finland integrate arts into STEM ("STEAM") with strong outcomes → Conclusion: False binary; creativity and analytical rigour are mutually reinforcing.', '🎯 Từ vựng: dichotomy, mutually reinforcing, analytical rigour, cohesion, pipeline, prioritisation, integration model, STEAM'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Câu hỏi chính sách (should governments...): State position clearly → 2-3 reasons → acknowledge counterargument → restate position.' } ] }, // =========================================================== // CAMBRIDGE IELTS 18 – FULL LISTENING (4 SECTIONS, 21 CÂU) // =========================================================== 'Cambridge IELTS 18 · Full Listening Test (4 Sections – 40 Câu)': { type: 'audio_mcq', audioTitle: 'Cambridge IELTS 18 – Official Listening Test (UK & Australian Native Speakers)', audioScript: `SECTION 1 – REGISTERING FOR A COMMUNITY EVENT Narrator: Section 1. You will hear a conversation between a resident, Helen, and a community centre coordinator registering for a local charity fundraising event. Coordinator: Good afternoon, Greenfield Community Centre, Jessica speaking. Helen: Hello, I'm calling to register for the charity 5K fun run next Saturday. Coordinator: Wonderful! May I take your full name? Helen: Yes, it's Helen Patricia Dawson. D-A-W-S-O-N. Coordinator: And your date of birth, for our age category records? Helen: The fourteenth of March, nineteen eighty-six. Coordinator: Perfect. And which distance category are you registering for — the five-kilometre, ten-kilometre, or the half-marathon? Helen: Just the five-kilometre this time — I'm getting back into running after a knee injury. Coordinator: Understood. The registration fee is twelve pounds fifty for adults. Would you like to include the optional charity t-shirt for an additional eight pounds? Helen: Yes, I'd love one! What sizes are available? Coordinator: We have extra small, small, medium, large, and extra large. Helen: I'll take a medium please. Coordinator: Wonderful. So that's twenty pounds fifty in total. We accept cash on the day or you can pay online via our website at www dot greenfield-community dot co dot uk. Helen: I'll pay online. Is there anything else I should know? Coordinator: Yes — participants should arrive by eight AM at Greenfield Park, Gate B. The route passes through the riverside area and finishes at the bandstand in the park centre. We provide water stations at the two-kilometre and four-kilometre marks. Please bring your registration confirmation email on your smartphone or printed. Helen: Great. And one more thing — is there parking nearby? Coordinator: Yes, there's a car park on Elm Street adjacent to the park — it's free on weekends. SECTION 2 – ECO-RESORT ORIENTATION TALK Narrator: Section 2. You will hear a welcome talk by the manager of a sustainable eco-resort. Manager: Welcome, everyone, to Rainforest Retreat — one of Southeast Asia's most highly-rated sustainable tourism destinations. I'm Marcus, your resort manager, and I'd like to give you a quick orientation before you settle into your lodges. The resort covers approximately forty-five hectares of protected rainforest. All our lodges are constructed from responsibly sourced bamboo and recycled timber, and are fully powered by our on-site solar array supplemented by micro-hydro generation from the adjacent stream. Your lodge number corresponds to the pathway colour on your resort map — blue pathways lead to the waterfall area, green pathways go to the organic farm and cooking school, and red pathways lead to the wildlife observation tower. I'd like to draw your attention to a few important guidelines. First, please do not bring food into the forest pathways as this attracts wildlife such as macaques and monitor lizards, which, while spectacular, can become aggressive when food-conditioned. Second, swimming in the natural pools is permitted only between seven AM and five PM when our trained lifeguards are on duty. Finally, all single-use plastics are prohibited on the resort. Reusable water bottles and tote bags are provided in your lodges. Our daily eco-activities begin at six thirty AM with a guided birdwatching walk. At ten AM we offer bamboo weaving workshops in the cultural centre, and every afternoon at three PM there's a guided medicinal plant walk through the rainforest. All activities are included in your accommodation rate. If you have any questions, the reception desk is staffed twenty-four hours a day. Enjoy your stay! SECTION 3 – ACADEMIC DISCUSSION: RESEARCH PROJECT ON CONSUMER PSYCHOLOGY Narrator: Section 3. You will hear two students, Rachel and Oliver, discussing their undergraduate research project on consumer decision-making. Rachel: Oliver, I've been thinking about our research question. Our professor suggested we narrow our focus to the effect of choice overload on consumer satisfaction — what do you think? Oliver: I think that's actually a really rich area. Barry Schwartz's paradox of choice research would be a solid theoretical foundation. Essentially, the more options consumers have, the lower their satisfaction, even if they ultimately choose what they wanted. Rachel: Exactly. I was thinking we could design a survey using the Likert scale to measure satisfaction across different shopping contexts — online versus in-store. Oliver: That's a good approach. However, I think we also need to control for individual differences in maximising versus satisficing tendencies. Maximisers — people who need to find the absolute best option — are disproportionately affected by choice overload compared to satisficers, who are content with a sufficiently good option. Rachel: Good point. Should we recruit participants through the university's psychology participant pool? Oliver: Yes, but we should make sure we have a balanced gender split and include both older and younger adult cohorts. Choice behaviour can vary significantly by age group. Rachel: What statistical tests do you plan to use for the analysis? Oliver: I'm thinking a two-way ANOVA to analyse the interaction effects between shopping context and personality type, with a follow-up Tukey's HSD post-hoc test if we find significant interactions. Rachel: That's quite sophisticated for an undergraduate project — are we confident we can execute that within our software competency? Oliver: I'll use SPSS — I attended a workshop on it last semester. It should be manageable if we keep our variable count reasonable. SECTION 4 – ACADEMIC LECTURE: BEHAVIOURAL ECONOMICS Narrator: Section 4. You will hear a lecture on behavioural economics. Lecturer: Good morning. Today's lecture addresses one of the most transformative intellectual developments in modern economics: the systematic integration of cognitive psychology into economic theory — what we now call behavioural economics. Classical economics rested on the foundational assumption of the rational actor — the homo economicus — who makes decisions by calculating expected utilities and consistently choosing outcomes that maximise self-interest. This elegant theoretical framework powered economic policy and corporate strategy for over two centuries. However, starting with the groundbreaking work of Israeli psychologists Amos Tversky and Daniel Kahneman in the 1970s and 80s, researchers began cataloguing a rich taxonomy of cognitive biases that demonstrably cause humans to deviate systematically from rational choice. Kahneman's dual-process theory, popularised in his 2011 book Thinking, Fast and Slow, distinguishes between System 1 — fast, intuitive, emotionally-driven processing — and System 2 — slow, deliberate, analytical reasoning. Most economic decisions, it turns out, are dominated by System 1. The anchoring effect demonstrates that humans are disproportionately influenced by the first piece of numerical information they encounter — a retail price tag of £200 struck through and replaced with £120 creates a powerful perception of value regardless of the product's intrinsic worth. Similarly, loss aversion — the finding that losses loom approximately twice as large as equivalent gains in human psychology — explains why investors hold onto depreciating stocks far longer than rational analysis would recommend. Perhaps most consequential for policy design is the concept of choice architecture: the finding that default options exercise enormous influence over human behaviour. When organ donation was made the default opt-out rather than opt-in option in Austria, donation rates exceeded ninety-nine percent compared to just twelve percent in neighbouring Germany where opt-in remained the default.`, questions: [ // SECTION 1 { text: 'What is the name of the caller registering for the event?', translated: 'Tên của người gọi đăng ký sự kiện là gì?', choices: ['Helen Patricia Dawson', 'Jessica Patricia Dawson', 'Helen Margaret Dawson', 'Helen Patricia Davidson'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Người gọi tự giới thiệu: "it\'s Helen Patricia Dawson. D-A-W-S-O-N."' }, { text: 'What is the total registration cost including the t-shirt?', translated: 'Tổng chi phí đăng ký bao gồm áo thun là bao nhiêu?', choices: ['£12.50', '£18.00', '£20.50', '£22.00'], answer: 2, ai_explain: '"The registration fee is twelve pounds fifty... optional charity t-shirt for an additional eight pounds... So that\'s twenty pounds fifty in total." £12.50 + £8.00 = £20.50.' }, { text: 'What time should participants arrive at the event?', translated: 'Người tham dự nên đến lúc mấy giờ?', choices: ['7:00 AM', '7:30 AM', '8:00 AM', '8:30 AM'], answer: 2, ai_explain: '"participants should arrive by eight AM at Greenfield Park, Gate B."' }, { text: 'Where is the car park for the event located?', translated: 'Bãi đậu xe nằm ở đâu?', choices: ['Inside Greenfield Park', 'Behind the community centre', 'On Elm Street adjacent to the park', 'Opposite the bandstand'], answer: 2, ai_explain: '"Yes, there\'s a car park on Elm Street adjacent to the park — it\'s free on weekends."' }, // SECTION 2 { text: 'What type of energy sources power the eco-resort?', translated: 'Nguồn năng lượng nào cung cấp điện cho khu nghỉ dưỡng sinh thái?', choices: ['Wind and geothermal', 'Solar and micro-hydro', 'Diesel generators and solar', 'Biomass and wind'], answer: 1, ai_explain: '"fully powered by our on-site solar array supplemented by micro-hydro generation from the adjacent stream."' }, { text: 'What colour pathways lead to the wildlife observation tower?', translated: 'Đường đi màu gì dẫn đến · Academic Reading Full Test (3 Passages – 40 Câu)': { type: 'reading_passage', passageTitle: 'Cambridge IELTS 18 – Academic Reading Full Test', passageText: `PASSAGE A: THE COGNITIVE SCIENCE OF BILINGUALISM For decades, educational psychologists operated under the paradigm that childhood bilingualism incurred substantial cognitive penalties. The "semilingual" hypothesis, dominant through the mid-twentieth century, posited that exposure to two linguistic systems simultaneously would fragment cognitive resources, producing children with inadequate mastery of either language. This view informed educational policy in many countries, discouraging bilingual instruction in favour of full immersion in the dominant language. However, contemporary neuroimaging research has fundamentally overturned this assumption. Researchers including Ellen Bialystok at York University, Toronto, have documented through longitudinal fMRI studies that negotiating two linguistic systems actively strengthens executive function — the brain's supervisory control system responsible for task switching, inhibitory control, and working memory capacity. This cognitive advantage, termed the "bilingual advantage," appears most pronounced in tasks requiring selective attention — the ability to focus on relevant information while suppressing distracting stimuli. Critically, bilingual individuals continuously suppress task-irrelevant phonemes and syntactical structures while engaging with one language, constituting perpetual neurological exercise. This cognitive workout builds what researchers term "cognitive reserve" — an enduring neurological buffer that delays symptomatic manifestations of age-related neurodegenerative conditions. A landmark 2007 study by Craik and Bialystok documented that bilingual patients received diagnoses of Alzheimer's dementia an average of 4.5 years later than matched monolingual controls, even after controlling for education, occupation, and immigration status. Nevertheless, critics caution against overstating these findings. Several independent meta-analyses, including a 2014 comprehensive review by Angela de Bruin in Psychological Science, found publication bias may have inflated effect sizes in positive bilingualism studies. The consensus position in cognitive neuroscience remains that bilingualism confers measurable but context-dependent cognitive benefits, with individual variation playing a significant moderating role. PASSAGE B: THE GLOBAL HISTORY OF COFFEE Coffee's journey from an Ethiopian highland plant to a globally traded commodity spanning cultural rituals and billion-dollar corporations constitutes one of economic history's most fascinating transformations. According to popular legend, the stimulatory properties of the coffee plant were first observed by an Ethiopian goatherd named Kaldi, who noticed his flock became unusually energetic after consuming the bright red berries of the Coffea arabica plant. While historically unverifiable, this narrative captures coffee's Ethiopian origins authentically: the wild ancestors of all commercial coffee plants are indeed endemic to the Kaffa region of Ethiopia. Coffee cultivation and trade were systematically developed by Yemeni traders in the port of Mocha from the fifteenth century onwards. The Sufi monasteries of Yemen used coffee preparations to enable extended nighttime religious devotion, and Ottoman coffeehouses — called qahveh khaneh — rapidly became centres of intellectual and political discourse. By the sixteenth century, Ottoman authorities had twice attempted to prohibit coffee, perceiving coffeehouses as hotbeds of sedition and intellectual dissent. European coffee culture arrived via the Ottoman Empire. The first coffeehouse in England opened in Oxford in 1650, and within two decades, over three hundred coffeehouses operated in London alone. These establishments — nicknamed "penny universities" because entry cost a single penny — were crucibles of Enlightenment thought, financial innovation, and scientific exchange. Lloyd's of London, the global insurance market, originated as a coffeehouse frequented by maritime merchants and ship captains. Brazil's emergence as the world's dominant coffee producer, supplying approximately one-third of global output, resulted from a combination of geographical fortune, brutal slave labour, and systematic deforestation of the Mata Atlântica coastal rainforest. Contemporary specialty coffee movements increasingly emphasise traceability, direct trade with smallholder farmers, and biodiversity-friendly shade-grown cultivation techniques as ethical responses to this extractive colonial legacy. PASSAGE C: AUTOMATION, ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND THE FUTURE OF LABOUR The relationship between technological innovation and employment has always been characterised by creative disruption. The nineteenth-century Luddite movement expressed organised resistance to mechanical looms that eliminated traditional textile workers' livelihoods, yet industrialisation ultimately generated far more jobs than it destroyed — albeit through painful transitional decades of structural unemployment. Today, economists and technologists debate whether artificial intelligence and automation represent a qualitative discontinuity from previous technological transitions. A 2013 Oxford Martin School study by Carl Benedikt Frey and Michael Osborne generated considerable alarm by estimating that approximately 47% of US occupations were at high risk of automation within two decades. Subsequent research has moderated this assessment. A 2016 OECD analysis applying a more granular task-based methodology found only 9% of jobs face high automation risk, as most occupations involve complex combinations of manual dexterity, social intelligence, and creative problem-solving that remain computationally intractable. The sectoral distribution of automation risk reveals pronounced inequalities. Routine cognitive tasks — data processing, paralegal research, basic financial analysis — face high displacement risk regardless of their educational prerequisites. By contrast, occupations characterised by interpersonal care (nursing, psychotherapy, early childhood education) and complex contextual judgment (surgery, strategic consulting, architectural design) demonstrate robust resistance to automation even as adjacent administrative tasks become computerised. Economic research increasingly points to polarisation: the hollowing out of middle-skill, middle-wage occupations while demand expands at both the high-skill/high-wage apex (AI specialists, data scientists, biotechnologists) and, more contentiously, the low-skill/low-wage base (care workers, delivery drivers, restaurant staff). Policy responses advocated by researchers range from investment in lifelong learning infrastructure and portable skills certification to proposals for universal basic income as a structural buffer [Town features 1975: Town Hall, Open Market, River, Single-lane bridge, Farmland (north), Forest (south). Town features 2025: New shopping centre (replaces open market), Multi-lane highway bridge, Residential suburbs (replaces farmland), Business park (replaces forest), Hospital (new), Train station (new)].', translated: 'Task 1: Hai bản đồ mô tả bố cục thị trấn nhỏ năm 1975 và 2025. Tóm tắt các thay đổi chính.', choices: [ '📋 DÀN Ý BAND 8.0: Câu 1 (Overview): The town underwent significant transformation. Câu 2 (Mở rộng): Commercial and residential expansion dominates. Body 1: Infrastructure changes (open market → shopping centre, single-lane → multi-lane bridge). Body 2: Land-use changes (farmland → suburbs, forest → business park) + new facilities (hospital, train station).', '✍️ BÀI MẪU BAND 8.5: "The two maps chronicle the substantial physical transformation of a small town across a fifty-year period, from 1975 to 2025. Overall, the town experienced pronounced commercial, infrastructural, and residential expansion, with natural and agricultural land substantially replaced by urban development throughout the illustrated period. In 1975, the town\'s character was predominantly rural. The central feature was an open market adjacent to the town hall, with a single-lane bridge connecting the settlement across the river. Agricultural land dominated the northern periphery, while a forested area occupied the southern zone. By 2025, the landscape had undergone fundamental restructuring. The open market was replaced by a modern shopping centre, reflecting the commercialisation of the town centre. The original single-lane river crossing was superseded by a multi-lane highway bridge, accommodating increased vehicular traffic. Most dramatically, the northern farmland was converted into residential suburbs, while the southern forest was cleared to accommodate a business park. Two entirely new facilities — a hospital in the eastern quadrant and a train station connecting the settlement to regional rail networks — were constructed during this period. In summary, the town transformed from a modest rural settlement to a substantially urbanised community characterised by commercial, residential, and industrial infrastructure." (224 từ — Band 8.5)', '🎯 TIÊU CHÍ MAP TASK 1 BAND 8.5: ✅ Clear overview of the dominant change (urbanisation) ✅ Accurate and comprehensive feature coverage ✅ Precise spatial language (northern, southern, eastern, adjacent, superseded) ✅ Appropriate passive voice for describing changes ✅ Logical chronological or spatial grouping' ], answer: 1, ai_explain: 'Map Task 1: Quan trọng nhất là ghi rõ vị trí địa lý (north, south, east, west) và dùng thì quá khứ/hiện tại để so sánh đúng.' }, { text: 'IELTS Academic Writing Task 2 (40 phút – ≥250 từ): Some educationalists argue that tertiary institutions should focus primarily on providing students with practical vocational skills directly applicable to the labour market. Others believe universities should maintain their traditional role of offering comprehensive academic education that cultivates critical thinking, regardless of immediate market utility. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.', translated: 'Task 2: Một số nhà giáo dục cho rằng đại học nên tập trung vào kỹ năng nghề nghiệp thực tiễn. Người khác tin đại học nên duy trì vai trò đào tạo học thuật toàn diện. Thảo luận cả hai quan điểm và nêu ý kiến của bạn.', choices: [ '📋 DÀN Ý 4 ĐOẠN BAND 8.0: Introduction: "The debate over the primary purpose of university education represents a fundamental tension between economic pragmatism and intellectual tradition." + Thesis: universities must pursue both, but with the critical thinking mandate serving as the unifying framework. Body 1: Case for vocational focus (labour market alignment, student debt ROI, industry partnership, Singapore polytechnic model). Body 2: Case for academic education (adaptability in disrupted labour markets, civil society participation, innovation driven by basic research). Conclusion: Both vocational competencies AND critical reasoning are essential; the dichotomy is false.', '✍️ BÀI MẪU BAND 8.5: "The ongoing pedagogical discourse concerning the fundamental mission of higher education encapsulates a broader societal tension between pragmatic economic imperatives and the humanistic traditions of liberal education. While both positions possess intrinsic merit, I contend that characterising these orientations as mutually exclusive fundamentally misrepresents the multifaceted obligations of the contemporary university. Proponents of a vocationally-oriented tertiary curriculum advance compelling arguments grounded in economic reality. As students accumulate substantial financial liabilities through tuition and student loans, the expectation that a degree confers measurable occupational readiness represents a reasonable contractual obligation. Nations such as Singapore and Germany have demonstrated that robust industry-university partnerships and structured apprenticeship integration produce graduates with immediately productive technical competencies and strong employment outcomes. Furthermore, in sectors experiencing rapid technological disruption, curricula that maintain close alignment with evolving industry standards provide graduates with genuine competitive advantage. Nevertheless, reducing the university to a professional training institution would constitute a profound institutional diminution. The capacity for rigorous analytical reasoning, historical contextualisation, and ethical judgment — cultivated through exposure to philosophy, literature, social science, and fundamental science — equips graduates not merely for their first employment, but for intellectual adaptability across the multiple career transitions that characterise contemporary working lives. The Oxford physicist who studies Homer is not wasting her time; she is cultivating a cognitive versatility that algorithmic routine cannot replicate. I therefore maintain that the most intellectually honest response to this debate is to reject the binary entirely. The optimal university curriculum integrates disciplinary vocational training within a broader liberal education framework, ensuring graduates possess both the technical fluency and the critical infrastructure to navigate — and meaningfully contribute to — an increasingly complex world." (293 từ — Band 8.5)', '🎯 TIÊU CHÍ TASK 2 BAND 8.5: ✅ Task Response: Thảo luận cả 2 + nêu lập trường rõ ràng ✅ Từ vựng C1: encapsulates, imperatives, diminution, contextualisation, versatility, binary ✅ Grammar: Gerund subjects, complex relative clauses, passive constructions ✅ Cohesion: Proponents of... / Nevertheless... / I therefore maintain...' ], answer: 1, ai_explain: 'Kiểu đề "Discuss both views and give opinion" yêu cầu Body 1 trình bày View A, Body 2 View B, kết hợp quan điểm của bạn trong cả phần kết luận.' }, { text: 'BAND BREAKDOWN & EXAMINER FEEDBACK SIMULATION – IELTS Writing Score Prediction: Nhập bài viết Task 2 của bạn để nhận đánh giá chi tiết theo 4 tiêu chí.', translated: 'Mô phỏng phản hồi của giám khảo IELTS: Phân tích bài viết Task 2 theo 4 tiêu chí.', choices: [ '📊 SELF-MARKING CHECKLIST TASK 2: TA (25%): Bài có trả lời đúng yêu cầu đề bài? Có nêu quan điểm rõ ràng? Có đủ 4 đoạn (Intro + 2 Body + Conclusion)? CC (25%): Liên từ có tự nhiên không? Mỗi đoạn có 1 idea chính? LR (25%): Ít nhất 10-15 từ vựng C1 không lặp lại? Không dùng từ "very/really/a lot"? GRA (25%): Có ít nhất 3 loại câu phức khác nhau? Ít hơn 2 lỗi ngữ pháp nghiêm trọng trên 250 từ?', '📊 COMMON BAND 6 → BAND 7 IMPROVEMENT TIPS: 1. Thay "nowadays" bằng "in the contemporary era / in recent decades". 2. Thay "I think" bằng "I contend / I maintain / It is my conviction that". 3. Thay "a lot of" bằng "a significant proportion of / an overwhelming majority of". 4. Mở bài không được dùng lại từ đề bài nguyên văn — phải paraphrase. 5. Mỗi Body paragraph cần có: Topic sentence + Explanation + Evidence/Example + Mini-conclusion.', '📊 EXAMINER INSIGHT – BAND 7 vs BAND 8 DIFFERENTIATOR: Band 7 viết đúng và rõ; Band 8 viết với sự tinh tế học thuật (nuance). Sự khác biệt thường nằm ở: (a) Lexical Precision — dùng đúng từ trong đúng collocations; (b) Grammatical Range — thể hiện đa dạng cấu trúc câu có chủ ý; (c) Coherence — ý tưởng liên kết mượt mà như luồng lập luận học thuật thực sự, không chỉ nối bằng liên từ.' ], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Tự đánh giá theo rubric là kỹ năng then chốt để tự học IELTS Writing hiệu quả mà không cần giáo viên chấm bài hàng ngày.' } ] }, // =========================================================== // CAMBRIDGE IELTS 18 – FULL SPEAKING (PART 1 + 2 + 3) // =========================================================== 'Cambridge IELTS 18 · Full Speaking Test (Part 1 + Part 2 + Part 3)': { type: 'speaking', questions: [ { text: 'Part 1, Q1: Do you enjoy spending time in nature? Why or why not?', translated: 'Part 1: Bạn có thích dành thời gian trong thiên nhiên không? Tại sao?', choices: ['💡 Structure Band 7.5+: "Absolutely — I find immersing myself in natural environments genuinely restorative. Living in a busy urban centre, I\'ve come to appreciate the psychological decompression that comes from hiking or simply sitting near a lake. There\'s compelling research suggesting that even brief periods in green spaces measurably reduce cortisol levels. I make a point of visiting the botanical gardens near my university every weekend."', '🎯 Key vocab: restorative, immerse myself in, psychological decompression, cortisol levels, green spaces, botanical'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Part 1 Nature questions: Nên kết hợp cảm xúc cá nhân + lý do khoa học/thực tế để câu trả lời phong phú hơn.' }, { text: 'Part 1, Q2: How often do you use public transport, and do you find it convenient?', translated: 'Part 1: Bạn có thường xuyên dùng phương tiện công cộng không và bạn thấy nó có tiện lợi không?', choices: ['💡 Structure Band 7.5+: State frequency → contextual reason → honest assessment → comparison or future vision. E.g., "I rely on public transport almost exclusively for daily commuting — I take the metro and occasionally the city bus. Frankly, the reliability has improved significantly since the new network expansion. However, I still find the last-mile connectivity during peak hours somewhat challenging — getting from the station to my workplace involves either a 20-minute walk or an unreliable shuttle service."', '🎯 Key vocab: rely on, commuting, reliability, last-mile connectivity, peak hours, network expansion'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Câu hỏi về thói quen hàng ngày: Dùng từ chỉ tần suất (almost exclusively, occasionally) và đánh giá cân bằng tích cực + hạn chế.' }, { text: 'Part 1, Q3: Do you prefer to work independently or in a team? Can you give an example?', translated: 'Part 1: Bạn thích làm việc độc lập hay theo nhóm? Bạn có thể đưa ra ví dụ không?', choices: ['💡 Template: "I\'d say I have a strong preference for collaborative work, though with important caveats. In my final-year research project, working with three teammates whose expertise complemented mine — one was strong in quantitative analysis, another in scientific writing — enabled us to produce a substantially more comprehensive study than any of us could have independently. That said, for creative writing or deep conceptual thinking, I find solitude essential."', '🎯 Key vocab: collaborative, complementary expertise, caveats, conceptual thinking, solitude, interdisciplinary'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Part 1 Work preference: Nêu lựa chọn rõ ràng → example cụ thể → thừa nhận ngoại lệ (nuance). Tránh nói chung chung.' }, { text: 'Part 1, Q4: What environmental habits have you personally adopted in your daily life?', translated: 'Part 1: Bạn đã thực sự áp dụng những thói quen môi trường nào trong cuộc sống hàng ngày?', choices: ['💡 Concrete examples Band 7.5: "I\'ve made a few deliberate lifestyle adjustments over the past year. I\'ve switched almost entirely to a plant-based diet during the week — research suggests this reduces my personal carbon footprint by roughly 30% compared to an omnivorous diet. I also carry a reusable coffee cup and shopping bag as a matter of course, and I\'ve started composting kitchen waste, which has reduced our household general waste by around 40%."', '🎯 Key vocab: deliberate adjustments, carbon footprint, plant-based, omnivorous, composting, household waste'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Câu hỏi về thói quen môi trường: Nêu ví dụ cụ thể với số liệu ước tính → thể hiện self-awareness and engagement.' }, { text: 'Part 1, Q5: Are there any traditional customs or festivals you particularly value in your culture?', translated: 'Part 1: Có phong tục truyền thống hay lễ hội nào trong văn hóa của bạn mà bạn đặc biệt trân trọng không?', choices: ['💡 Structure: Name specific festival/custom → describe it briefly → personal significance → connection to cultural identity. E.g., "Tết — the Vietnamese Lunar New Year — holds deep personal significance for me. Beyond the festive surface of firecrackers and red envelopes, it\'s fundamentally an occasion for familial reconciliation and gratitude. There\'s a tradition of thoroughly cleaning the home before Tết — symbolically sweeping away the misfortunes of the past year — which I find profoundly meaningful as a ritual of psychological renewal."', '🎯 Key vocab: cultural identity, familial reconciliation, ritual, psychological renewal, festive, symbolically'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Câu hỏi về văn hóa và phong tục: Đi sâu vào ý nghĩa cá nhân thay vì chỉ mô tả bề mặt.' }, // PART 2 – Cue Card { text: 'Part 2 – Cue Card (1 phút chuẩn bị, 2 phút nói): Describe an environmental law or regulation in your country that you believe is particularly effective. You should say: • What it is; • When and why it was introduced; • What changes it has brought about; and explain • Why you consider it effective or important.', translated: 'Part 2 Cue Card: Miêu tả một đạo luật hoặc quy định môi trường ở quốc gia bạn mà bạn cho là đặc biệt hiệu quả.', choices: ['✍️ BÀI MẪU BAND 8.0 (2 PHÚT): "I\'d like to describe Vietnam\'s national ban on single-use non-biodegradable plastic bags in retail and food service environments, which came into partial effect from 2026 as part of the country\'s Environmental Protection Law revision. The legislation was introduced primarily in response to Vietnam\'s status as one of the world\'s largest contributors to marine plastic pollution — a classification driven by rapid economic development that had outpaced waste management infrastructure. The practical outcomes, though still early in implementation, have been encouraging. Major supermarket chains have transitioned to paper bags and reusable canvas alternatives, while the hospitality sector has widely adopted biodegradable packaging. Consumer behaviour surveys conducted six months after implementation showed a 42% reduction in single-use bag consumption in urban centres. What I consider most significant is not merely the immediate environmental impact, but the normative shift in consumer consciousness. Younger urban residents, in particular, have adopted reusable bags not merely as legal compliance, but as a marker of environmental identity and civic responsibility. Of course, enforcement in rural markets and informal food stalls remains inconsistent, and the legislation would benefit from stronger financial penalties and accompanying public education campaigns. Nevertheless, as a policy intervention that has visibly altered both business practices and consumer behaviour within a relatively short timeframe, I consider it a genuinely meaningful environmental achievement." (245 từ — Band 8.0)', '🎯 PHÂN TÍCH CUE CARD: ✅ All 4 bullet points addressed ✅ Specific statistics (42% reduction) ✅ Balanced assessment (acknowledges enforcement gaps) ✅ Personal connection (normative shift in consciousness) ✅ Vocabulary: non-biodegradable, normative shift, civic responsibility, enforcement, implementation'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Cue Card môi trường: Tránh nói quá chung chung "protect the environment." Hãy chọn một luật/quy định CỤ THỂ và đánh giá nó một cách cân bằng.' }, // PART 3 { text: 'Part 3, Q1: Do you believe individual consumer choices can meaningfully address climate change, or do structural governmental policies need to take precedence?', translated: 'Part 3: Bạn có tin rằng các lựa chọn tiêu dùng cá nhân có thể giải quyết có ý nghĩa vấn đề biến đổi khí hậu không, hay các chính sách cấu trúc của chính phủ cần được ưu tiên hơn?', choices: ['💡 Lập luận phức tạp Band 8.0: Acknowledge individual action matters but critique "personal responsibility" framing → argue that fossil fuel companies have historically promoted individualism to deflect structural accountability → carbon footprint concept itself was popularised by BP → systemic change requires carbon pricing, infrastructure investment, international agreements → individuals matter most as political actors (voting, advocacy) rather than as consumers.', '🎯 Vocab: structural accountability, carbon pricing, systemic change, advocacy, deflect, proliferate, regulatory frameworks, Paris Agreement'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Part 3 câu này có chiều sâu chính trị/kinh tế: Đừng chỉ nói "both are important" mà environmental challenges?', translated: 'Part 3: Bạn nghĩ các thỏa thuận quốc tế như Hiệp định Paris về khí hậu có hiệu quả như thế nào trong việc giải quyết các thách thức môi trường toàn cầu?', choices: ['💡 Balanced critique Band 8.0: Acknowledge significance (first legally binding universal climate framework, 196 signatories, NDC mechanism) → identify structural weaknesses (non-binding emissions targets, enforcement absence, US withdrawal under Trump administration, equity concerns for developing nations) → positive impact (accelerated renewable energy investment, corporate net-zero pledges) → overall verdict: important normative framework but insufficient without stronger enforcement mechanisms.', '🎯 Vocab: legally binding, Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), normative framework, enforcement mechanisms, equity concerns, signatories, net-zero pledges'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Câu hỏi về hiệp định quốc tế: Cần biết ít nhất 2-3 chi tiết cụ thể (tên điều khoản, số liệu, ví dụ quốc gia) để đạt Band 8.0.' }, { text: 'Part 3, Q3: In your view, should businesses be legally required to adopt sustainable practices, or should environmental responsibility remain voluntary?', translated: 'Part 3: Theo bạn, các doanh nghiệp có nên bị yêu cầu pháp lý phải áp dụng thực hành bền vững không, hay trách nhiệm môi trường nên là tự nguyện?', choices: ['💡 Structure lập luận: State position (mandatory frameworks are necessary) → evidence 1 (voluntary CSR has failed — major corporations still increase emissions under voluntary pledges) → evidence 2 (mandatory carbon disclosure laws in EU showing positive results) → acknowledge concern (regulatory burden on SMEs, competitiveness) → nuance (proportionate regulation, phased implementation, green investment incentives alongside mandates) → restate conclusion.', '🎯 Vocab: mandatory frameworks, corporate social responsibility (CSR), carbon disclosure, regulatory burden, SMEs, phased implementation, green investment incentives, proportionate regulation'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Câu hỏi mandatory vs voluntary: Luôn tránh lập trường tuyệt đối. Nêu mandatory là cần thiết nhưng thừa nhận cần thiết kế chính sách thông minh.' }, { text: 'Part 3, Q4: How do you think younger generations differ from older generations in their attitudes toward environmental issues?', translated: 'Part 3: Theo bạn, thế hệ trẻ và thế hệ lớn tuổi khác nhau như thế nào trong thái độ với các vấn đề môi trường?', choices: ['💡 Intergenerational analysis Band 8.0: Younger generations (Gen Z, Millennials) demonstrate heightened environmental concern (Fridays for Future, school strikes) and integrate sustainability into purchasing identity → reasons: climate anxiety is a lived daily experience, not a future abstraction; social media amplifies environmental consciousness; growing up with IPCC reports as context. Older generations: environmental concern exists but often framed through economic lens; scepticism of systemic overhaul; nostalgia for industrial prosperity. Nuance: generational generalisation is imprecise — class, education, geography matter as much.', '🎯 Vocab: intergenerational, climate anxiety, Fridays for Future, consumption identity, environmental consciousness, IPCC, economic lens, industrial prosperity, generational generalisation'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Câu hỏi so sánh thế hệ: Hãy cite ví dụ phong trào cụ thể (Greta Thunberg, Fridays for Future) và giải thích nguyên nhân tâm lý xã hội.' }, { text: 'Part 3, Q5: Do you think that economic development and environmental protection can be achieved simultaneously, or are they inevitably in conflict?', translated: 'Part 3: Bạn có nghĩ rằng phát triển kinh tế và bảo vệ môi trường có thể đạt được đồng thời không, hay chúng không thể tránh khỏi mâu thuẫn với nhau?', choices: ['💡 Sophisticated argument Band 8.0: Reject false dichotomy → Green Growth hypothesis evidence (Denmark, Germany: GDP growth + carbon reduction simultaneously) → acknowledge limits: decoupling is relative not absolute; material throughput eventually encounters planetary boundaries → concept of Doughnut Economics (Kate Raworth): redesign economies around social foundation and ecological ceiling → conclusion: conflict exists when growth is measured only by GDP; reconceptualising economic success metrics is the key.', '🎯 Vocab: false dichotomy, decoupling, material throughput, planetary boundaries, Doughnut Economics, ecological ceiling, GDP, reconceptualise, green growth, sustainable development'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Câu hỏi triết học kinh tế-môi trường: Demonstrate knowledge of Doughnut Economics or Green New Deal concepts = instant Band 8.0+ credibility.' } ] }, // Bài luyện ngắn (Practice) 'IELTS Listening · Section 1: Form Completion': { type: 'audio_mcq', audioTitle: 'IELTS Listening Practice – Section 1: Hotel Booking Form', audioScript: 'Agent: Thank you for calling Lakeside Hotel. Have you decided on your sampling methodology? Mei: We\'re considering stratified random sampling across three districts — high-income, middle-income, and low-income residential zones. 2, ai_explain: '"We\'re aiming for 450 participants across the three zones — 150 each."' } ] }, 'IELTS Reading · Academic: Matching Headings': { type: 'reading_passage', passageTitle: 'IELTS Reading Practice: The Psychology of Colour in Marketing', passageText: 'A. Research in consumer psychology consistently demonstrates that colour exerts a profound influence on purchasing behaviour, operating largely beneath the threshold of conscious awareness. Studies suggest that colour accounts for up to 90% of snap product judgments within the first 90 seconds of initial exposure, making chromatic design one of the most powerful tools in a marketer\'s arsenal.\n\nB. Colour associations are not universal; they are substantially mediated by cultural context. White, the conventional symbol of purity and simplicity in Western markets, functions as the colour of mourning and funerary ritual in many East Asian cultural contexts. Similarly, green — associated with environmental consciousness and natural health in European markets — carries associations of illness and misfortune in some Indonesian communities.\n\nC. Luxury brands systematically exploit colour psychology to signal prestige and exclusivity. Deep navy, burgundy, and matte black communicate sophistication through their association with restraint and understatement. By contrast, fast food corporations overwhelmingly favour combinations of red and yellow — colours psychologically associated with urgency, appetite stimulation, and energy — to accelerate customer throughput and discourage lingering.\n\nD. Colour consistency across brand touchpoints — packaging, digital platforms, retail environments, and advertising — creates what marketers term "colour equity": the proprietary value embedded in a distinctive chromatic identity. The distinctive red of Coca-Cola\'s branding is so culturally embedded that the company\'s Christmas advertising is widely credited with popularising the modern image of Santa Claus in a red suit.', questions: [ { text: 'Which heading best matches Paragraph A?', translated: 'Tiêu đề nào phù hợp nhất với đoạn A?', choices: ['The cultural relativity of colour meaning', 'Colour\'s rapid and powerful influence on consumer decisions', 'How luxury brands use colour for exclusivity', 'Building brand value through chromatic consistency'], answer: 1, ai_explain: 'Đoạn A tập trung vào nghiên cứu tâm lý tiêu dùng: màu sắc ảnh hưởng đến 90% quyết định mua hàng trong 90 giây đầu.' }, { text: 'Which heading best matches Paragraph B?', translated: 'Tiêu đề nào phù hợp nhất với đoạn B?', choices: ['The translated: 'Tiêu đề nào phù hợp nhất với đoạn C?', choices: ['Building brand value through chromatic consistency', 'How colour communicates brand personality and sector identity', 'The cultural
