interpretation', 'Building brand value through chromatic consistency', 'Colour\'s rapid influence on purchasing decisions', 'Colour psychology in luxury marketing'], answer: 1, ai_explain: 'Đoạn D về "colour equity" — giá trị thương hiệu được xây dựng qua tính nhất quán của màu sắc (ví dụ: đỏ Coca-Cola).' }, { text: 'According to Paragraph A, what percentage of initial product judgments are influenced by colour?', translated: 'Theo đoạn A, bao nhiêu phần trăm các phán đoán sản phẩm ban đầu bị ảnh hưởng bởi màu sắc?', choices: ['Up to 50%', 'Up to 70%', 'Up to 90%', 'Up to 100%'], answer: 2, ai_explain: '"colour accounts for up to 90% of snap product judgments within the first 90 seconds of initial exposure."' }, { text: 'What colour associations do fast food brands typically leverage?', translated: 'Các thương hiệu đồ ăn nhanh thường tận dụng liên kết màu sắc nào?', choices: ['Blue and green for calm and health', 'Red and yellow for urgency and appetite', 'Black and gold for luxury', 'White and silver for cleanliness'], answer: 1, ai_explain: '"fast food corporations overwhelmingly favour combinations of red and yellow — colours psychologically associated with urgency, appetite stimulation, and energy."' } ] }, 'IELTS Reading · True / False / Not Given': { type: 'reading_passage', passageTitle: 'IELTS Reading Practice: The History and Science of Sleep', passageText: 'Sleep, long dismissed by productivity-obsessed cultures as mere biological necessity, is increasingly recognised by neuroscientists as a period of extraordinary neurological activity. During slow-wave sleep, the glymphatic system — a recently discovered neural waste clearance mechanism — flushes metabolic by-products including amyloid-beta proteins from the brain\'s interstitial fluid. Accumulation of these proteins is strongly associated with the development of Alzheimer\'s disease, providing a compelling mechanistic explanation for the long-documented correlation between chronic sleep deprivation and elevated dementia risk.\n\nHistorically, pre-industrial humans did not sleep in the consolidated eight-hour block contemporary sleep medicine prescribes. Historian Roger Ekirch\'s landmark research, drawing on pre-industrial diaries, court records, and literary sources, documented a bi-phasic sleep pattern common until the widespread adoption of artificial lighting in the nineteenth century. People would sleep for approximately four hours, awaken for an hour or two of quiet activity — prayer, conversation, or even visits to neighbours — before returning to a second sleep of equal duration.\n\nContemporary research underscores the non-negotiable nature of adequate sleep for peak cognitive function. A 2003 study by Hans Van Dongen demonstrated that individuals restricted to six hours of sleep per night for two weeks showed cognitive impairments equivalent to those produced by two full nights of total sleep deprivation — yet rated themselves as only "slightly sleepy", demonstrating a dangerous insensitivity to accumulating sleep debt.', questions: [ { text: 'The glymphatic system was already well understood by neuroscientists before the 20th century.', translated: 'Hệ thống glymphatic đã được các nhà khoa học thần kinh hiểu rõ trước thế kỷ 20.', choices: ['TRUE', 'FALSE', 'NOT GIVEN'], answer: 1, ai_explain: 'FALSE. Bài đọc gọi nó là "a recently discovered neural waste clearance mechanism" — được phát hiện gần đây, không phải từ lâu.' }, { text: 'Chronic sleep deprivation has been linked to an increased risk of Alzheimer\'s disease.', translated: 'Thiếu ngủ mãn tính đã được liên kết với nguy cơ mắc bệnh Alzheimer tăng cao.', choices: ['TRUE', 'FALSE', 'NOT GIVEN'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'TRUE. "the long-documented correlation between chronic sleep deprivation and elevated dementia risk."' }, { text: 'Pre-industrial people typically slept for twelve or more hours per day.', translated: 'Người tiền công nghiệp thường ngủ 12 giờ hoặc hơn mỗi ngày.', choices: ['TRUE', 'FALSE', 'NOT GIVEN'], answer: 1, ai_explain: 'FALSE. Bài đọc mô tả giấc ngủ hai pha: "approximately four hours... before returning to a second sleep of equal duration" = tổng cộng ~8 giờ, không phải 12 giờ.' }, { text: 'The shift from bi-phasic to monophasic sleep coincided with the spread of artificial lighting.', translated: 'Sự chuyển đổi từ giấc ngủ hai pha sang một pha trùng với sự phổ biến của ánh sáng nhân tạo.', choices: ['TRUE', 'FALSE', 'NOT GIVEN'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'TRUE. "until the widespread adoption of artificial lighting in the nineteenth century."' }, { text: 'People restricted to six hours of sleep accurately perceived their cognitive impairment.', translated: 'Những người bị hạn chế ngủ 6 tiếng nhận thức chính xác về sự suy giảm nhận thức của họ.', choices: ['TRUE', 'FALSE', 'NOT GIVEN'], answer: 1, ai_explain: 'FALSE. Họ "rated themselves as only \'slightly sleepy\', demonstrating a dangerous insensitivity to accumulating sleep debt" — không nhận biết được mức độ suy giảm thực sự.' }, { text: 'The 2003 Van Dongen study tested participants who were completely deprived of sleep for six hours.', translated: 'Nghiên cứu Van Dongen năm 2003 thử nghiệm với những người bị thiếu ngủ hoàn toàn trong 6 giờ.', choices: ['TRUE', 'FALSE', 'NOT GIVEN'], answer: 1, ai_explain: 'FALSE. Nghiên cứu hạn chế ngủ 6 tiếng/đêm trong 2 tuần ("restricted to six hours of sleep per night for two weeks"), không phải thiếu ngủ hoàn toàn.' } ] }, 'IELTS Writing · Task 2: Opinion Essay': { type: 'writing', questions: [ { text: 'IELTS Writing Task 2 (40 phút – ≥250 từ): Some people believe that universities should make attendance at lectures and seminars compulsory for all students. Others argue that students should have the freedom to choose whether to attend classes. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.', translated: 'Task 2: Một số người cho rằng đại học nên bắt buộc sinh viên tham dự bài giảng và seminar. Những người khác cho rằng sinh viên nên có tự do lựa chọn. Thảo luận cả hai và nêu ý kiến của bạn.', choices: [ '📋 DÀN Ý CẤU TRÚC BAND 7.5+: Introduction: Paraphrase + thesis (I maintain that while voluntary attendance has merit for advanced learners, structured attendance frameworks are essential for the majority of undergraduates). Body 1 FOR compulsory (academic rigour, social learning, reduced procrastination, staff accountability). Body 2 FOR voluntary (adult autonomy, flexible learning styles, online resource equivalence, individual responsibility). Body 3/Conclusion: Own position + nuanced recommendation (differentiated policy by year level or course type).', '✍️ BAND 7.5 BOUNDING PARAGRAPH (intro + conclusion): Opening: "The question of whether university attendance should be institutionally mandated or voluntarily self-regulated touches upon fundamental tensions between academic authority and individual autonomy. While proponents of voluntary attendance invoke principles of personal responsibility and learning flexibility, I contend that structured attendance requirements, thoughtfully implemented, better serve the developmental needs of most undergraduate students, particularly in their formative academic years." Conclusion: "In summary, the binary between compulsory and voluntary attendance obscures a more nuanced reality: optimal policy design would mandate attendance in first and second year — when academic habits and social belonging are being established — while affording greater flexibility to students in advanced study programmes who have demonstrably cultivated independent scholarly discipline."', '🎯 VOCABULARY BANK FOR THIS TOPIC: institutionally mandated / voluntarily self-regulated / pedagogical scaffold / academic rigour / autonomous learner / procrastination / synchronous learning environment / asynchronous digital resources / formative years / cultivate scholarly discipline / demonstrably / differentiated policy' ], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Discuss both + opinion: 3-body structure = Body 1 (View A pros), Body 2 (View B pros), Body 3 (own nuanced synthesis). Avoid simplistic "both have advantages and disadvantages."' }, { text: 'IELTS Writing Task 2 (40 phút – ≥250 từ): In many countries, an increasing number of people are choosing to live alone. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this trend? Give your own opinion about the main effects of this social change.', translated: 'Task 2: Ở nhiều quốc gia, ngày càng có nhiều người chọn sống một mình. Ưu điểm và nhược điểm của xu hướng này là gì? Nêu ý kiến của bạn về tác động chính của sự thay đổi xã hội này.', choices: [ '📋 ADVANTAGES: 1. Complete autonomy over lifestyle decisions (diet, schedule, social commitments); 2. Dedicated space for deep work and intellectual focus; 3. Stronger sense of self-sufficiency and personal identity; 4. Reduced interpersonal conflict and compromise fatigue.', '📋 DISADVANTAGES: 1. Social isolation and loneliness epidemic (WHO designates loneliness as a global public health threat); 2. Economic inefficiency (higher per-capita housing, energy, food costs); 3. Reduced social support network during health crises; 4. Environmental impact (single-occupancy homes have higher carbon footprint per resident).', '🎯 BAND 8.0 OPINION SYNTHESIS: "On balance, I believe single-person household growth reflects genuinely positive social evolution — the expansion of individual autonomy, particularly for women and marginalised communities historically constrained by cohabitation norms — but necessitates countervailing social infrastructure: co-housing communities, robust public social spaces, and mental health support frameworks to prevent the pathological isolation that unmitigated solitary living can precipitate." Vocabulary: precipitate, countervailing, cohabitation, pathological isolation, social infrastructure, autonomy.' ], answer: 2, ai_explain: 'Kiểu đề Advantages & Disadvantages + Opinion: Phải bao gồm CẢ HAI phía và đưa ra lập trường cuối cùng. Band 8.0 không chỉ liệt kê — cần phân tích hàm ý xã hội.' } ] }, 'IELTS Speaking · Part 2 & 3: Cue Card': { type: 'speaking', questions: [ { text: 'Part 1 Warm-up: What kind of music do you enjoy listening to?', translated: 'Part 1: Bạn thích nghe thể loại nhạc nào?', choices: ['💡 "I tend to gravitate toward indie folk music — artists like Sufjan Stevens and Bon Iver. What draws me to this genre is the lyrical sophistication and the emotional intimacy of the acoustic arrangements. I find it particularly conducive to focused studying or reflective evening walks." Từ vựng: gravitate toward, lyrical sophistication, acoustic arrangements, conducive to, reflective'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Music Part 1: Link to personal emotion + activity context = richer, more memorable answer.' }, { text: 'Part 2 Cue Card: Describe an interesting place you have visited. You should say: where it is; when you went there; what you did there; and explain why you found it particularly interesting or memorable.', translated: 'Part 2 Cue Card: Miêu tả một địa điểm thú vị bạn đã đến thăm. Nêu nơi đó ở đâu, khi nào bạn đến, bạn đã làm gì ở đó, và giải thích tại sao bạn thấy nó đặc biệt thú vị hoặc đáng nhớ.', choices: ['✍️ BAND 7.5 SAMPLE (1.5 phút): "I\'d like to describe my visit to Hội An Ancient Town in central Vietnam, which I experienced for the first time during a solo travel trip approximately two years ago. What distinguished this destination from conventional tourist sites was its extraordinary architectural palimpsest — the town preserves over 1,000 classified heritage structures representing five centuries of Vietnamese, Chinese, Japanese, and French colonial architectural influence, creating an urban environment of remarkable visual layering. During my three-day visit, I explored the Japanese Covered Bridge — a sixteenth-century pedestrian bridge that serves simultaneously as a cultural landmark and a Shinto shrine — wandered through the lantern-lit old quarter after sunset, and participated in a traditional Vietnamese cooking class where I learned to prepare bánh xèo, the celebrated sizzling pancake. What made the visit particularly memorable was the town\'s capacity to feel simultaneously ancient and vibrantly alive — the heritage structures are not museum exhibits but functioning shops, family homes, and restaurants, creating an experience of living history rarely encountered in such an authentic form." (191 từ — Band 7.5)', '🎯 Từ vựng cue card địa điểm: architectural palimpsest, heritage structures, visual layering, landmark, Shinto shrine, vibrantly alive, functioning, living history, simultaneously'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Place Cue Card: Chọn địa điểm bạn thực sự biết và có câu chuyện cụ thể. Tránh nói các địa điểm nổi tiếng quá phổ biến mà không có góc nhìn độc đáo.' }, { text: 'Part 3, Q1: Do you think tourism benefits or harms the cultural heritage of destinations?', translated: 'Part 3: Bạn có nghĩ du lịch mang lại lợi ích hay tổn hại cho di sản văn hóa của các điểm đến?', choices: ['💡 Analysis Band 8.0: "The relationship between tourism and cultural heritage is genuinely dialectical — tourism simultaneously provides the economic justification for heritage preservation and generates the visitor pressure that most directly threatens it. The Venice paradox encapsulates this: the city attracts 25 million visitors annually, generating revenues essential for maintaining its architectural fabric, yet the volume has created structural damage, pricing out resident communities whose cultural vitality is itself a heritage asset. Sustainable tourism frameworks — visitor caps, dispersal strategies, community benefit sharing — represent the most promising reconciliation of these competing interests."', '🎯 Vocab: dialectical, paradox, architectural fabric, pricing out, resident communities, sustainable tourism, dispersal strategies, community benefit sharing'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Part 3 Heritage question: Avoid simply "yes/no" — the dialectical (hai chiều mâu thuẫn nội tại) framing demonstrates sophisticated analytical thinking.' }, { text: 'Part 3, Q2: Should governments invest more in preserving historical sites or in building new infrastructure for modern communities?', translated: 'Part 3: Chính phủ nên đầu tư nhiều hơn vào việc bảo tồn các địa điểm lịch sử hay xây dựng cơ sở hạ tầng mới cho cộng đồng hiện đại?', choices: ['💡 False dichotomy approach: "I\'d resist framing this as a binary choice, since heritage preservation IS contemporary infrastructure — cultural and psychological infrastructure. The economic case for heritage investment is robust: UNESCO estimates that creative and cultural industries contribute $2.25 trillion annually to global GDP. But beyond economics, historical sites provide communities with narrative continuity — a sense of temporal depth and collective identity that purely functional infrastructure cannot supply. A society that understands its history is better equipped to navigate its future. The most productive policy approach integrates adaptive reuse: repurposing heritage structures for contemporary community functions, preserving cultural fabric while meeting modern needs."', '🎯 Vocab: binary choice, temporal depth, collective identity, narrative continuity, adaptive reuse, heritage investment, UNESCO, cultural industries'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Part 3 Policy question: Reject the false binary + make the case that heritage IS a form of infrastructure = sophisticated position that earns high marks.' }, { text: 'Part 3, Q3: How has international travel changed the way people view their own culture?', translated: 'Part 3: Du lịch quốc tế đã thay đổi cách con người nhìn nhận văn hóa của chính họ như thế nào?', choices: ['💡 Anthropological lens Band 8.0: Travel creates the "defamiliarisation" effect — experiencing radically different cultural frameworks makes visible what one previously took for granted as universal. A European who experiences communal multi-generational family living in Vietnam or India may return home with a newly critical eye on individualistic domestic norms. Conversely, travel can equally produce cultural reaffirmation — encountering challenges abroad heightens appreciation for elements of home culture previously undervalued. The net effect is typically a more nuanced, less ethnocentric worldview, though this outcome is not automatic — it depends on the quality and depth of cultural engagement during travel.', '🎯 Vocab: defamiliarisation, ethnocentric, cultural reaffirmation, communal living, individualistic norms, anthropological, cultural engagement, nuanced worldview'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Part 3 câu về tác động văn hóa của du lịch: Concept "defamiliarisation" (xa lạ hóa cái quen thuộc) là một góc nhìn học thuật mạnh để nâng tầm câu trả lời.' }, { text: 'Part 3, Q4: Do you think it is important for young people to travel before settling into a career?', translated: 'Part 3: Bạn có nghĩ điều quan trọng là những người trẻ nên đi du lịch trước khi bắt đầu sự nghiệp không?', choices: ['💡 Position + nuance: "I think travel in young adulthood can be profoundly formative, but I\'d caution against treating it as a universal prescription. For individuals who have had limited exposure to diversity — whether cultural, socioeconomic, or geographical — extended travel can accelerate cognitive flexibility and empathic development in ways that formal education rarely replicates. The gap year research is genuinely positive in this regard. However, I\'d distinguish between purposeful travel with reflective intentionality — volunteering, language immersion, cross-cultural work experience — and mere tourism, which can paradoxically reinforce existing assumptions by exposing travellers only to surfaces rather than depths."', '🎯 Vocab: profoundly formative, cognitive flexibility, empathic development, gap year, purposeful travel, reflective intentionality, language immersion, paradoxically reinforce'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Part 3 gap year question: Distinguish types of travel (purposeful vs tourism) + cite relevant research (gap year studies) = Band 8.0 level reasoning.' }, { text: 'Part 3, Q5: In what ways has globalisation changed the cultural landscapes of cities around the world?', translated: 'Part 3: Toàn cầu hóa đã thay đổi cảnh quan văn hóa của các thành phố trên thế giới theo những cách nào?', choices: ['💡 Critical globalisation analysis: Acknowledge homogenisation (international architectural styles, global franchise dominance, fashion convergence, English linguistic hegemony) → BUT also argue for cultural creolisation and hybridity — local cultures do not passively receive global influence but actively negotiate and blend it (Korean pop music incorporating global EDM while maintaining distinctly Korean sonic and visual aesthetics; Japanese ramen incorporating Italian pasta techniques). The most productive framing: globalisation does not destroy cultural diversity but redistributes it, creating new hybrid forms alongside diminished traditional ones. The key policy question is whether indigenous communities retain agency in this process.', '🎯 Vocab: homogenisation, linguistic hegemony, creolisation, hybridity, sonic aesthetics, indigenous communities, agency, franchise dominance, cultural negotiation'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'Part 3 Globalisation & Culture: The concept of "creolisation/cultural hybridity" (không phải tiêu diệt mà lai tạo) là phân tích tinh tế nhất và đạt điểm cao nhất.' } ] }, // Cambridge IELTS 18 Academic Reading Practice – Bilingualism (luyện ngắn) 'Cambridge IELTS 18 · Academic Reading: True / False / Not Given & Headings': { type: 'reading_passage', passageTitle: 'Cambridge 18 Academic Passage: Cognitive Science of Bilingualism & Early Education', passageText: `For decades, educational psychologists operated under the paradigm that childhood bilingualism incurred substantial cognitive penalties. The "semilingual" hypothesis, dominant through the mid-twentieth century, posited that exposure to two linguistic systems simultaneously would fragment cognitive resources, producing children with inadequate mastery of either language. However, contemporary neuroimaging research has fundamentally overturned this assumption. Researchers including Ellen Bialystok at York University have documented through longitudinal fMRI studies that negotiating two linguistic systems actively strengthens executive function — the brain's supervisory control system responsible for task switching, inhibitory control, and working memory capacity. Bilingual individuals continuously suppress task-irrelevant phonemes and syntactical structures while engaging with one language, constituting perpetual neurological exercise. This cognitive workout builds "cognitive reserve" — an enduring neurological buffer. A landmark 2007 study documented that bilingual patients received diagnoses of Alzheimer's dementia an average of 4.5 years later than matched monolingual controls.`, questions: [ { text: 'Early twentieth-century psychologists believed that raising children bilingually hindered their intellectual development.', translated: 'Các nhà tâm lý học đầu thế kỷ 20 tin rằng việc nuôi dạy trẻ song ngữ cản trở sự phát triển trí tuệ của chúng.', choices: ['TRUE', 'FALSE', 'NOT GIVEN'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'TRUE. "educational psychologists operated under the paradigm that childhood bilingualism incurred substantial cognitive penalties."' }, { text: 'According to research, bilingualism delays symptoms of Alzheimer\'s dementia by approximately 4.5 years.', translated: 'Theo nghiên cứu, việc biết hai ngôn ngữ làm chậm các triệu chứng sa sút trí tuệ Alzheimer trung bình 4.5 năm.', choices: ['TRUE', 'FALSE', 'NOT GIVEN'], answer: 0, ai_explain: 'TRUE. "bilingual patients received diagnoses of Alzheimer\'s dementia an average of 4.5 years later than matched monolingual controls."' }, { text: 'Children who acquire three languages develop stronger executive control than bilingual peers.', translated: 'Trẻ em học ba ngôn ngữ phát triển khả năng kiểm soát điều hành mạnh hơn bạn bè song ngữ.', choices: ['TRUE', 'FALSE', 'NOT GIVEN'], answer: 2, ai_explain: 'NOT GIVEN. Bài đọc chỉ nghiên cứu người song ngữ, không đề cập so sánh với người học ba ngôn ngữ.' }, { text: 'What neurological ability is specifically stimulated when a bilingual person suppresses the inactive language?', translated: 'Khả năng thần kinh nào được kích thích cụ thể khi người song ngữ ức chế ngôn ngữ không hoạt động?', choices: ['Inhibitory control and executive function.', 'Auditory musical pitch identification.', 'Peripheral vision spatial mapping.', 'Rapid mathematical computation.'], answer: 0, ai_explain: '"negotiating two linguistic systems actively strengthens executive function... responsible for task switching, inhibitory control, and working memory capacity."' } ] } }; // ========================================== // 3. THANG QUY ĐỔI BAND ĐIỂM CHUẨN IDP / BC // ========================================== function calculateIeltsBand(rawScore, totalQuestions) { if (!totalQuestions || totalQuestions === 0) totalQuestions = 40; const percentage = (rawScore / totalQuestions) * 100; let band = 5.0; if (percentage >= 90) band = 9.0; else if (percentage >= 87) band = 8.5; else if (percentage >= 80) band = 8.0; else if (percentage >= 75) band = 7.5; else if (percentage >= 67) band = 7.0; else if (percentage >= 60) band = 6.5; else if (percentage >= 52) band = 6.0; else if (percentage >= 43) band = 5.5; else band = 5.0; let descriptor = 'Competent User'; if (band >= 8.5) descriptor = 'Expert / Very Good User (C2)'; else if (band >= 7.5) descriptor = 'Very Good User (C1)'; else if (band >= 6.5) descriptor = 'Good / Competent User (B2)'; else descriptor = 'Modest User (B1)'; return { band, descriptor, percentage: Math.round(percentage) }; } // Export window.ieltsCourses = ieltsCourses; window.ieltsExams = ieltsExams; window.calculateIeltsBand = calculateIeltsBand; })(window);
